message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 181, "amount_cents": 17092}, {"order_id": 184, "amount_cents": 3930}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the orders and refunds myself, since the handoff only reports that refunds were applied.
Orders are listed, and I need to check the refunds list too before computing payouts. Refund 181 (17092) and 184 (3930) were reported, so I'll verify them against the ledger.
The refunds ledger matches W2's handoff exactly (181 and 184), so the refund data checks out. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 27136 matches its orders (16857 + 10279) with no refunds, so the data is consistent. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 19909 matches its orders (26275 + 14656 = 40931) minus refunds 181 and 184 (17092 + 3930 = 21022), so the figures agree. Cobalt has no refunds, so I'll check its net balance next.
Cobalt's net of 31469 matches its orders (26600 + 4869) with no refunds, so all three customers reconcile with the ledger. I'll record acme's payout of 27136 first.
Acme's payout of 27136 is recorded. Birch's net of 19909 matches orders minus refunds, so I'll record that payout next.

Cobalt's net of 31469 matches its orders (26600 + 4869) with no refunds, and all three balances reconcile with the ledger. Acme and birch are already recorded, so I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three customers have been paid, and each net balance matched the orders minus refunds from the ledger. The batch is complete.
